# Review of SEEN-109, attempt 2, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned on opus with the task text of triage record 24 and nothing else. It read
the ticket, all twenty-four records and the seventeen files of the focus set,
plus `harness/kpi.py`, `harness/templates/review.json` and both calibration
report files. `reviewer_session` is null for the reason note 17 gives.

Verdict: **return**, on F1.

It confirmed the four findings of the first review as genuinely answered, and
that the RED at record 19 fails for the reasons record 23 states.

## The findings

**F1, high, `harness/calibration.py:219`.** `_covers` still strips the
characters `.` and `/` from a slice's planned files rather than the prefix
`./`: the same bug the ticket was returned on at record 18, surviving one
function below the docstring written to explain it, and the last `lstrip('./')`
in `harness/`. It sits on the other side of the same comparison and decides the
route verdict rather than the triage one. A finding in a dot-directory file is
charged to no slice, so a downgraded slice that produced it reads as having
produced nothing, and findings are the only per-slice measure the route rule
has. SEEN-104 and SEEN-105 planned slices over `.claude/`, `.codex/` and
`.agents/` paths, and no test exercised a slice file outside `harness/`.

**F2, medium, `harness/calibration.py:207`.** Findings were read only from an
advance out of review, so a high or blocking finding that returned a ticket
counted only if the session repeated it in the record that finally passes, which
no gate requires. What saved it was convention: SEEN-104, SEEN-105 and SEEN-108
each carried every earlier round's findings forward.

**F3, medium, `harness/calibration.py:428`.** Criterion 3's second half, the
founder's decision recorded in the journal of the ticket that flips the switch,
was met by prose in three documents and by nothing in the harness: anyone could
set `triage_shadow = false` and the next triage would narrow with no record
anywhere of the decision, the evidence behind it or who took it.

**F4, low, `harness/thresholds.toml`.** `counted_from` read
`2026-09-25T20:00:00+00:00` while the commit that added the section landed at
20:08:27, so the boundary was eight minutes earlier than the comment and the
Outcome both say. Latent, because no journal starts inside that window, and it
is the value the ticket's headline claim rests on.

**F5, low, `docs/harness/history/SEEN-109/0007.json`.** Slice 1 predicted two
REDs and only the first is recorded. Check 7 fails with the ImportError every
test in the new file produces, so it proves the module was absent and not that
the review gate was permissive. The behaviour is covered today, so this is a
hole in the evidence rather than in the code.

## The deterministic checks it was handed

`red_before_green` passes for slice 2 and for attempt 2, where the cited
failures match the stated reasons word for word, and is partial for slice 1 for
the reason F5 gives. `tests_added` passes, with the note that no test exercised
a slice whose planned files sit in a dot directory, which is what let F1
survive. `acceptance_entries` passes. `slice_files` it passed for the same
reason the first review did. `pull_request` stayed unavailable.

It also checked the ground rules over the whole diff: no euro sign, no dashes,
no browser automation, no live marketplace host, no table, no credential, no
buyer PII, no agent action, British spelling throughout.

## What the shadow window will read from this round

F1 lands in `harness/calibration.py`, which triage record 24 kept, so it is not
an escape; the rest are medium or low and cannot be. The round reads clean, and
the ticket is excluded from the window by name in any case.
